title: tune: NCCL streams & scheduling to improve overlap of collectives with compute (tp, kvcache, continuous batching)
author: Sanjay Patel
description: Motivation: Multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads show suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and GPU kernels when using KV cache + continuous batching. This manifests as higher p99 latency and lower sustained throughput for long-sequence generation workloads. This PR applies a set of coordinated changes to improve overlap and reduce kernel/collective stalls across TP shards. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce prioritized NCCL stream assignment for collectives used in TP all-reduce/all-gather so that communication runs on dedicated streams with adjustable priorities. 2) Add a small scheduler in runtime/kernel_scheduler.cpp to prefer launching GPU kernels on the compute stream without forcing implicit syncs when collectives are active; kernels that can safely run concurrently are dispatched on non-blocking streams. 3) Rework KV cache access patterns to avoid implicit CUDA event waits: KV cache evictions and prefetches now use an explicit async API and respect stream priorities, lowering cross-stream synchronization. 4) Continuous batching flow updated to align batch formation timestamps with KV cache readiness windows; the batching manager will delay forming a new micro-batch by up to a configurable hysteresis if a KV prefetch/collective is still outstanding, improving locality and reducing tail latency jitter. 5) Add heuristics to fall back to a synchronized path on GPUs that report poor peer-to-peer connectivity (windows for problematic hardware). Results: steady-state throughput +8% on our internal TP-4 (A100x8) benchmark for 2k-token generation, median latency unchanged, p99 latency down ~12% across synthetic long-sequence workloads, and a small (2-3%) reduction in peak GPU memory due to earlier eviction scheduling. Backwards compatibility and safety: All behavioral changes are behind runtime flags and config toggles (defaults enabled for newly provisioned Dedicated fleets after rollout). The PR includes perf tests and a small e2e test that replays a representative workload to validate correctness and numerical parity. See linked Linear tasks for rollout plan and tuning knobs.

review_comments: Laura Chen: Nice focused set of changes. Can you justify default stream priorities and include a note about starved low-priority kernels?

Sanjay Patel: Default priorities are chosen after sweeping on TP-4 (A100x8); we place NCCL on higher-priority stream to avoid collectives getting deferred. Low-priority kernels are limited to non-critical maintenance work; added comment and flag to revert to equal priorities.
Diego Alvarez: KV async prefetch looks good but I'm concerned about subtle ordering bugs across streams. Do you have asserts or debug-only checks?

Sanjay Patel: Added cudaEvent checks in debug builds and an e2e replay that validated ordering for ~50k generated tokens across 10 runs. Also added a regression test that injects a fake slow peer and verifies fallback to sync path.
Maya Singh: CI perf showed one flaky run with worse p99; did you rerun?
Sanjay Patel: Yes, perf CI was flaky due to a noisy host during the first run; re-run completed and numbers are stable. Added CI note to ignore runs with >10% host CPU contention.
